exposure: induction of labor at 39 weeks 0 days to 39 weeks 6 days
expectant management with delivery from 40 weeks 0 days to 42 weeks 6 days
outcome: maternal morbidity composite (uterine rupture, operative vaginal delivery, peripartum hysterectomy, intensive care unit admission, transfusion)
neonatal morbidity composite (neonatal intensive care unit admission, Apgar score less than 5 at 5 minutes, immediate ventilation, prolonged ventilation, seizure or serious neurological dysfunction)
cohort: The study cohort comprised 198,797 low-risk individuals in the US with vertex, singleton pregnancies and one prior cesarean delivery, excluding those with prior vaginal deliveries, deliveries outside of 39 weeks 0 days to 42 weeks 6 days, or medical comorbidities.
finding: Elective induction of labor at 39 weeks in low-risk patients with one prior cesarean delivery was associated with a significantly higher likelihood of vaginal delivery compared to expectant management, with no difference in composite maternal and neonatal morbidity outcomes.
mod_finding: Induction of labor at 39 weeks was associated with a higher likelihood of vaginal delivery, but also an increased likelihood of operative vaginal delivery among those who achieved vaginal birth.
gest_age: Included deliveries between 39 weeks 0 days and 42 weeks 6 days, with exposure groups defined by induction at 39 weeks 0 days to 39 weeks 6 days versus expectant management with delivery from 40 weeks 0 days to 42 weeks 6 days.
